RSA.name: RSA (Rivest-Shamir-Adleman)
RSA.quantum_attack: Shor's Algorithm (Polynomial-time prime factorization using quantum Fourier transform)
RSA.quantum_impact_description: A Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer (CRQC) running Shor's algorithm can factor n=p*q in O((log n)^3) quantum operations, completely breaking RSA private key recovery and signature forgery.
RSA.security_status: Vulnerable to CRQC. Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) risk for encrypted data.
RSA.performance_considerations: PQC signatures (ML-DSA) feature faster signing and verification than RSA-4096, but produce larger public keys (~1,312 bytes) and signatures (~2,420 bytes).
RSA.compatibility_considerations: Legacy TLS and X.509 cert chains may need packet fragmentation adjustments or dual-cert support during transition.

ECC.name: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (Generic / ECDSA / ECDH)
ECC.quantum_attack: Shor's Algorithm for Discrete Logarithms over Elliptic Curve Groups (ECDLP)
ECC.quantum_impact_description: Shor's algorithm solves discrete log on elliptic curves in O(log^3 N) operations, requiring only ~2,330 logical qubits to break 256-bit ECC.
ECC.security_status: Vulnerable to CRQC. Immediate HNDL threat for ECDH session keys.
ECC.performance_considerations: ML-KEM and ML-DSA provide 5x-10x faster computational throughput than ECC, though public keys and ciphertexts are larger (ML-KEM-768 ciphertext is 1,088 bytes vs 64 bytes for ECDH).
ECC.compatibility_considerations: Requires supporting larger frame sizes in network protocols and APIs.

ECDSA.name: ECDSA (Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm)
ECDSA.quantum_attack: Shor's Algorithm (Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem)
ECDSA.quantum_impact_description: CRQC allows forging valid signatures by recovering private keys from public keys and known signatures.
ECDSA.security_status: Vulnerable to CRQC. High urgency for long-lived code signing certificates and identity roots.

recommended_pqc_alternatives.Digital Signature: ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) [Primary General Purpose] or SLH-DSA-128s (FIPS 205) [Stateful/Stateless Hash-based for Root CAs]

hybrid_alternatives.Digital Signature: Hybrid Composite Dual Signature (ECDSA P-256 + ML-DSA-65)

ECDSA.performance_considerations: Verification is very fast in ML-DSA. SLH-DSA has higher CPU verification overhead but ultra-conservative hash-only security assumptions.
ECDSA.compatibility_considerations: X.509 RFC 9758 and RFC 9759 for composite signatures.

ECDH.name: ECDH (Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman)
ECDH.quantum_attack: Shor's Algorithm on Diffie-Hellman Discrete Logarithm
ECDH.quantum_impact_description: Adversaries can record TLS/VPN encrypted traffic today and decrypt it once a quantum computer is available (Harvest Now, Decrypt Later).
ECDH.security_status: Immediate HNDL risk for sensitive, high-longevity data.

hybrid_alternatives.Key Agreement: X25519 + ML-KEM-768 (Hybrid KEX standard deployed in OpenSSH, Chrome, and Cloudflare)

ECDH.performance_considerations: Extremely fast encapsulation/decapsulation (< 0.1 ms). Adds ~1 KB to TLS ClientHello/ServerHello.
ECDH.compatibility_considerations: TLS 1.3 draft extensions and OpenSSH 9.0+ natively support X25519MLKEM768.

Diffie-Hellman.name: Diffie-Hellman (DH / FFDH)
Diffie-Hellman.quantum_attack: Shor's Algorithm (Finite Field Discrete Logarithm Problem)
Diffie-Hellman.quantum_impact_description: CRQC solves finite field DLP in polynomial time, breaking shared secret derivation.
Diffie-Hellman.security_status: Critical vulnerability to HNDL. Finite field DH is also computationally slower than modern options.

hybrid_alternatives.Key Agreement: Hybrid FFDHE-3072 + ML-KEM-768 or X25519 + ML-KEM-768

Diffie-Hellman.performance_considerations: ML-KEM is 100x faster than FFDH-3072 and uses smaller key sizes.

Ed25519.name: Ed25519 (Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm over Curve25519)
Ed25519.quantum_impact_description: Curve25519 has 128-bit classical security, broken by Shor's algorithm with ~2,000 logical qubits.
Ed25519.security_status: Vulnerable to CRQC. Must be migrated for long-term authentication and signatures.

Ed448.name: Ed448 (Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm over Curve448)
Ed448.quantum_impact_description: Vulnerable to polynomial-time discrete log on quantum computers.
Ed448.performance_considerations: ML-DSA-87 delivers NIST Level 5 security with fast verification.

X25519.name: X25519 (ECDH Key Exchange over Curve25519)
X25519.quantum_impact_description: Recorded session handshakes can be broken retroactively by a CRQC.
X25519.security_status: Vulnerable to CRQC. Highest priority for HNDL mitigation.
X25519.performance_considerations: Hybrid combination adds only ~1,100 bytes and under 0.2ms overhead.
X25519.compatibility_considerations: Active industry standard in Chromium, Apple iOS 18+, Cloudflare, and OpenSSH.

AES.name: AES (Advanced Encryption Standard)
AES.quantum_attack: Grover's Algorithm (Quantum search reduces effective key strength by square root: O(2^(k/2)))
AES.quantum_impact_description: Grover's algorithm halves effective bit security. AES-128 offers 64-bit quantum security (marginal for top-secret/long-life data). AES-256 offers 128-bit quantum security, which remains computationally infeasible to break for the foreseeable future.
AES.security_status: AES-256 is QUANTUM-RESISTANT. AES-128 should be upgraded to AES-256 for long-lifetime classified data.

recommended_pqc_alternatives.Bulk Encryption: Upgrade AES-128 to AES-256-GCM (No PQC algorithm required for symmetric bulk encryption)

hybrid_alternatives.Bulk Encryption: AES-256-GCM / ChaCha20-Poly1305 with PQC-encapsulated symmetric keys (ML-KEM-768)

AES.performance_considerations: Hardware AES-NI provides > 10 GB/s throughput. Negligible overhead switching 128 to 256 bit.
AES.compatibility_considerations: Broad universal hardware and software support.

3DES.name: 3DES (Triple Data Encryption Standard / Triple-DES)
3DES.quantum_attack: Grover's Algorithm + Classical Sweet32 64-bit block collision
3DES.quantum_impact_description: Classically deprecated by NIST (SP 800-131A). Grover reduces effective security of 112-bit 3DES to 56 bits, well within quantum breakability.
3DES.security_status: Deprecated & Insecure. Immediate classical and quantum replacement required.
3DES.performance_considerations: AES-256 is 10x-50x faster due to hardware acceleration.
3DES.compatibility_considerations: Must update legacy hardware and banking data formats.

DES.name: DES (Data Encryption Standard)
DES.quantum_attack: Trivially broken classically (56-bit exhaustive search) and Grover reduction to 28 bits.

ChaCha20.name: ChaCha20 / ChaCha20-Poly1305
ChaCha20.quantum_impact_description: 128 bits of post-quantum security remains unbreakable.

recommended_pqc_alternatives.Bulk Encryption: Maintain ChaCha20-Poly1305 (Combine with ML-KEM for key exchange)

hybrid_alternatives.Bulk Encryption: ChaCha20-Poly1305 with ML-KEM-768 derived symmetric keys

ChaCha20.performance_considerations: High performance in software without dedicated hardware AES instructions.

SHA-1.name: SHA-1 (Secure Hash Algorithm 1)
SHA-1.quantum_attack: Brassard-Høyer-Tapp (BHT) Quantum Collision Finding + SHAttered Classical Collision
SHA-1.quantum_impact_description: Classically broken collisions (SHAttered, 2017). Quantum BHT algorithm finds collisions in O(2^(n/3)) = O(2^53) operations.
SHA-1.performance_considerations: SHA-256 and SHA-512 offer high performance on 64-bit systems.
SHA-1.compatibility_considerations: Replace all SHA-1 signature algorithms and HMACs.

MD5.name: MD5 (Message Digest 5)
MD5.quantum_impact_description: Completely vulnerable to collision and preimage attacks.

SHA-256.name: SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit)
SHA-256.quantum_attack: BHT Algorithm (Quantum collision: O(2^(256/3)) = ~2^85 operations; Grover Preimage: 2^128 operations)
SHA-256.quantum_impact_description: Quantum collision resistance is ~85-128 bits, safe for standard commercial applications. For top-tier NSA CNSA 2.0 security, SHA-384/512 is recommended.

recommended_pqc_alternatives.Hashing: Maintain SHA-256 or upgrade to SHA-384 / SHA-512 for CNSA 2.0 compliance

hybrid_alternatives.Hashing: SHA-256 + SHA3-256 dual hashing if desired

SHA-256.performance_considerations: Hardware acceleration available (Intel SHA extensions, ARMv8 Crypto).

SHA-384.name: SHA-384
SHA-384.quantum_impact_description: Provides full 128-bit quantum collision resistance and 192-bit preimage resistance.

recommended_pqc_alternatives.Hashing: Meets all Post-Quantum Requirements (NIST & NSA CNSA 2.0 compliant)

SHA-512.name: SHA-512
SHA-512.quantum_attack: Quantum collision security >= 170 bits; Grover preimage 256 bits.

TLS.name: TLS (Transport Layer Security Protocol)
TLS.quantum_attack: HNDL attack on classical Ephemeral Key Exchange (ECDHE/DHE)
TLS.quantum_impact_description: Network traffic captured today can be stored and decrypted when quantum computers arrive.
TLS.security_status: TLS 1.2/1.3 with classical KEX is vulnerable to HNDL. Must adopt Hybrid PQC KEX.

recommended_pqc_alternatives.Protocol: TLS 1.3 with Hybrid ML-KEM-768 Key Exchange (X25519Kyber768 / X25519MLKEM768) and ML-DSA-65 certificate chains

hybrid_alternatives.Protocol: Hybrid TLS 1.3: Classical ECDH (X25519) + PQC KEM (ML-KEM-768)

TLS.performance_considerations: Minimal latency delta (~1-2% increase in handshake size).
TLS.compatibility_considerations: Supported in BoringSSL, OpenSSL 3.2+ with oqsprovider, and Cloudflare/Google networks.

SSH.name: SSH (Secure Shell Protocol)
SSH.quantum_attack: HNDL on SSH session key exchange and quantum forgery of SSH host/user keys.
SSH.quantum_impact_description: Encrypted remote sessions captured over public networks can be decrypted in the future.
SSH.security_status: OpenSSH 9.0+ defaults to sntrup761x25519-sha512 hybrid KEX; OpenSSH 9.9+ integrates ML-KEM.

recommended_pqc_alternatives.Protocol: SSH-2 with mlkem768x25519-sha512 key exchange and ssh-mldsa65 authentication keys

SSH.performance_considerations: Negligible impact on interactive terminal latency.

ML-KEM.name: ML-KEM (Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism, FIPS 203 / CRYSTALS-Kyber)
ML-KEM.quantum_attack: Hardness based on the Module Learning With Errors (M-LWE) lattice problem, resistant to known classical and quantum algorithms.
ML-KEM.quantum_impact_description: NIST primary standard for post-quantum key encapsulation (FIPS 203 approved August 2024).

recommended_pqc_alternatives.Target: Primary post-quantum key establishment standard (ML-KEM-768 corresponds to NIST Security Level 3).

ML-KEM.performance_considerations: Extremely fast keygen, encapsulation, and decapsulation (< 50 microseconds). Public key: 1,184 bytes; Ciphertext: 1,088 bytes.
ML-KEM.compatibility_considerations: IETF RFC draft standardization for TLS 1.3, IKEv2, and SSH.

ML-DSA.name: ML-DSA (Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm, FIPS 204 / CRYSTALS-Dilithium)
ML-DSA.quantum_attack: Hardness based on Module Short Integer Solution (M-SIS) and M-LWE lattice problems.
ML-DSA.quantum_impact_description: NIST primary standard for general-purpose post-quantum digital signatures (FIPS 204 approved August 2024).

recommended_pqc_alternatives.Target: Primary general-purpose post-quantum digital signature standard.

ML-DSA.performance_considerations: Very fast signing and verification. Public key: 1,952 bytes; Signature: 3,309 bytes.
ML-DSA.compatibility_considerations: Requires updating certificate profile sizes in X.509 chains.

SLH-DSA.name: SLH-DSA (Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Algorithm, FIPS 205 / SPHINCS+)
SLH-DSA.quantum_attack: Security relies strictly on standard cryptographic hash functions (SHA-2, SHAKE), avoiding algebraic lattice assumptions.
SLH-DSA.quantum_impact_description: Ultra-conservative backup signature standard with minimal theoretical risk (FIPS 205 approved August 2024).
SLH-DSA.security_status: OFFICIALLY STANDARDIZED NIST PQC BACKUP STANDARD (FIPS 205).

recommended_pqc_alternatives.Target: Ideal for Root CAs, firmware signing, and environments requiring zero algebraic structure.

SLH-DSA.performance_considerations: Signatures are larger (~7.8 KB to 49 KB) and signing is slower than ML-DSA, but relies only on secure hash properties.
SLH-DSA.compatibility_considerations: Best suited for infrequent signing (e.g., firmware releases, root CAs).
